correctness.rationale: For every finite connected simple d-regular graph with d>=2 and h>0, pairs can meet at each of two home sites if adjacent and at each common-neighbor site. Exact binomial/Bernoulli occupancy conditional laws give a_d and b_d; solo occupancy gives s_d. Site summation proves W=s_d I+a_d A+b_d(A^2-dI), normalization per realized group implies stochasticity, symmetry is evident. The derivative of s_d is a positive factor times (h-1). Under triangle-freeness the edge weight is a_d; its derivative equals twice [(1-x)^(d-1)(2-(d+1)x)-1] for x=1/(h+d), and this bracket has one simple root. Strict Bernoulli inequality yields h_d*>d. The d=2 radical and large-d Lambert limit follow algebraically. Independently enumerating actual subsets for six finite graphs at four rational fidelities verified all 1044 matrix entries, row sums, and an exact triangular-prism comparison. General conclusions follow from analytic proof, not finite tests.

originality.rationale: The model and universal group-weight sum are established, not novel. A literature-led specialization yields an all-regular-graph quadratic adjacency-matrix identity, graph-independent temperature, common-neighbor corrections, and a sharp three-way separation of home-fidelity maxima for every degree at least two. Detailed comparisons with the primary 2026 completely-mixed article, the general 2020/2021 mathematical framework, the 2019 complex-network work, the 2024 community work, and the 2025 complete-network predictors did not locate an analytic equivalent, although a less accessible general weight specialization remains a genuine residual risk.
residual_risks: The 2020/2021 universal group-sum formula makes this statement derivable; an unlocated previous analytical specialization for regular networks could establish an equivalent theorem.
The 2019 numerical study and older graph-evolution literature contain many subcases; not every specialist paper or supplementary appendix is guaranteed indexed or accessible.
The static replacement-weight extrema do not imply optimal cooperation or fixation probabilities, which can depend strongly on the game and updating rules.

value.rationale: The source motivation links temperature and interindividual replacement weights to changes in social-game dynamics. This structural result resolves an exact, biologically interpretable distinction between maximizing an individual’s interaction rate, maximizing the chance adjacent residents encounter, and maximizing actual group-diluted replacement influence. The unique optimizers 1, d and h_d*>d hold for all degrees d>=2 and all triangle-free regular graphs; the all-regular adjacency-square identity exposes exact triangle-mediated edge heterogeneity hidden by identical vertex temperatures, with a rational triangular-prism witness. The object/invariant and downstream relevance precede the computation, and the result is not promoted as a fixation or cooperation theorem.
